Class LongestCommonSubsequence

Namespace
F23.StringSimilarity
Assembly
F23.StringSimilarity.dll

The longest common subsequence (LCS) problem consists in finding the longest subsequence common to two (or more) sequences. It differs from problems of finding common substrings: unlike substrings, subsequences are not required to occupy consecutive positions within the original sequences.

It is used by the diff utility, by Git for reconciling multiple changes, etc.

The LCS distance between Strings X (length n) and Y (length m) is n + m - 2 |LCS(X, Y)| min = 0 max = n + m

LCS distance is equivalent to Levenshtein distance, when only insertion and deletion is allowed (no substitution), or when the cost of the substitution is the double of the cost of an insertion or deletion.

! This class currently implements the dynamic programming approach, which has a space requirement O(m * n)!

public class LongestCommonSubsequence : IStringDistance, ISpanDistance

Distance<T>(ReadOnlySpan<T>, ReadOnlySpan<T>)

Calculates the distance between two sequences based on their similarity.

public double Distance<T>(ReadOnlySpan<T> s1, ReadOnlySpan<T> s2) where T : IEquatable<T>

Parameters

s1 ReadOnlySpan<T>

The first sequence to compare. Cannot be empty or null.

s2 ReadOnlySpan<T>

The second sequence to compare. Cannot be empty or null.

Returns

double

A non-negative double representing the distance between the two sequences. Returns 0 if the sequences are identical.

Type Parameters

T

The type of elements in the sequences. Must implement IEquatable<T>.

Remarks

The distance is calculated as the sum of the lengths of the two sequences minus twice the length of their longest common subsequence.

Exceptions

ArgumentNullException

Thrown if s1 or s2 is null.
